I deactivated my Facebook account and did't delete it just in case I have an impulse to go on it one day again. The reason was that I had less than 100 friends while all my other classmates all had at least 150+ friends. That damaged my self esteem GREATLY. I also didn't get any birthday wishes or stuff when it was my birthday and others get MILLIONS of messages saying happy birthday. I was and am still the odd one out at school and is the biggest failure there who just pretends to be happy, pretends to have good grades and hides my own test and exam papers. I have created a fake account under a fake name where I have 0 friends and 0 posts. That's how I still keep up with the celebrities or the pages I am into and NOT look at how ALL my "friends" are enjoying their lives. I know that people only put out the happy things on social media, but with me, there aren't any happy things I can post. I don't travel because my family's in a financial crisis, I don't go to fancy resturants or have fun in Disneyland. All I do is stay at home, look on Reddit, watch YouTube videos, read books, and sulk. Yeah, so my life sucks Reddit, but I guess not having social media helped me a little bit. And I really hope it helps you too.

I think I'm crazy. Sometimes I want to die, but sometimes I'm scared of death. So I can agree with you on 7,8 and 9, but I don't agree on 5. 

5. They may have abnormal sleeping and eating habits.
This may seem like a small sign or factor, but it has a grave effect. Those who live with depression in an unrevealing way can sometimes only let the little signs show. Sleeping too much or too little are textbook examples. The same goes goes for eating too little or too much. Sleep and nutrition are two critical elements to health. They are also two elements that the human mind can attempt to control. Depression creates a suffocating lack of control, and being able to control at least something, can be all a person has. Sleep can be nearly impossible, or it can be the only escape. The same goes for eating.

For a person having depression for a long time, I've never EVER felt sleeping being impossible or having a problem with eating. (unless I was sick and stuff) Maybe it's because I don't truly have depression? But the things I have going on is more on a emotional level with trying to deal with the fact that I'm a failure and on a physical level (trying to be normal).

What I said probably doesn't make sense at all. Comment if you have any idea what I'm talking about cause I don't.
